presentation_title: The Anatomy of a Good Prompt (The 3 C's)
episode: 2.1: The Anatomy of a Good Prompt (The 3 C's)
learning_objectives: Identify the three key ingredients of an effective prompt: Clarity, Context, and Constraints.
Apply Clarity, Context, and Constraints to transform weak prompts into strong ones.
Evaluate prompts to improve their effectiveness using the 3 C's framework.
prerequisites: Basic understanding of how to interact with AI models or chatbots.

slides.title: Weak Prompts Get Weak Answers
content: Have you ever asked an AI a question?
Did the answer feel vague or unhelpful?
A weak prompt often leads to a weak answer.
slides.narration:
Have you asked an AI a question?
Did you get a vague or unhelpful answer?
This often happens when our prompts are not clear enough.
A weak prompt will almost always give you a weak answer.
slides.image_prompt: Cartoon of a person scratching their head, looking confused at a computer screen showing generic text. A question mark thought bubble above their head.

slides.title: The 3 C's of a Good Prompt
content: Good prompts have three key ingredients:
1. Clarity: Be specific.
2. Context: Give background.
3. Constraints: Set rules.
slides.narration:
The best prompts, however, almost always include three key ingredients.
We call these the 3 C's: Clarity, Context, and Constraints.
Let's explore each of these in detail.
slides.image_prompt: A graphic showing three interconnected circles, each labeled with one of the '3 C's': Clarity, Context, Constraints. A central 'Good Prompt' icon.

slides.title: 1. Clarity: Be Specific!
content: First, let's talk about Clarity.
Being specific helps the AI understand your needs.
Vague prompts give generic, unhelpful answers.
slides.narration:
Let's start with Clarity.
Clarity means being specific in your request.
The AI cannot read your mind.
Vague prompts lead to generic and unhelpful answers.
slides.image_prompt: Cartoon illustration of a person holding a magnifying glass, looking closely at a clear, bright lightbulb.

slides.title: AI Can't Read Your Mind
content: Imagine talking to a new friend.
If you are vague, they won't understand.
The AI is similar; it needs clear instructions.
slides.narration:
Think about it like this:
If you ask a new friend a vague question, they might not understand.
The AI is similar.
It needs clear, precise instructions to give you the best response.
slides.image_prompt: Cartoon of two friends talking, one looking confused with a question mark, the other pointing clearly at something. Speech bubbles show clear vs. vague communication.

slides.title: Weak Prompt Example
content: Let's see a weak prompt:
"Write about electric cars."
What do you think the AI will write?
slides.narration:
Let's look at a weak prompt example.
If you simply type, 'Write about electric cars,' what kind of output do you expect?
It's very broad, isn't it?
slides.image_prompt: A cartoon person typing 'Write about electric cars.' into a chatbot interface. The chatbot's reply area shows a generic, long block of text.

slides.title: Reflection: What's Missing?
content: Pause and think.
What information is missing here?
What should the AI focus on?
slides.narration:
Pause and think about this prompt.
What information is missing?
What specific aspect of electric cars should the AI focus on?
This vagueness makes it hard for the AI to give you a useful answer.
slides.image_prompt: Cartoon of a person with a thought bubble showing '?' and '...' over their head, looking contemplatively at a screen.

slides.title: Improving with Clarity
content: Now, let's make it clear.
Add specific details to your request.
Tell the AI exactly what you need.
slides.narration:
Now, let's improve this prompt by adding clarity.
You need to tell the AI exactly what you need.
Also, state what details it should include.
This makes your request precise.
slides.image_prompt: Close-up cartoon of hands typing on a keyboard, with a screen showing a new, more detailed prompt being written.

slides.title: Clear Prompt Example
content: Here is a clear prompt:
"Write a short blog post explaining the top 3 benefits of owning an electric car for someone living in a city."
See the difference? Much clearer now!
slides.narration:
Here is a clear prompt.
It asks to write a short blog post.
This post should explain the top 3 benefits of owning an electric car.
It is for someone living in a city.
See the difference?
This prompt is much clearer.
It guides the AI to a specific topic and audience.
slides.image_prompt: Side-by-side comparison. Left: Weak prompt and generic output. Right: Clear prompt and a focused, bulleted output about electric car benefits in a city.

slides.title: 2. Context: Give Background!
content: Next, let's add Context.
Context tells the AI why you are asking.
It also defines the audience and perspective.
slides.narration:
Next, let's add Context.
Context tells the AI why you are asking this question.
It helps the AI adopt the right perspective.
It also helps understand who the audience is.
slides.image_prompt: Cartoon illustration of a person pointing to a background scene or a timeline, indicating 'background information'.

slides.title: Why Context Matters
content: Imagine asking for directions.
Knowing your destination (context) helps.
AI also needs this background information.
slides.narration:
Think about asking for directions.
If you just say 'Go straight,' it is not helpful.
Instead, say 'Go straight towards the market from the bus stop.'
That provides context.
AI needs this background to give relevant answers.
slides.image_prompt: Cartoon of a person giving directions to another, pointing down a path. Thought bubble above the recipient shows a map with a clear destination.

slides.title: Prompt Without Context
content: Recall our clear prompt:
"Write a short blog post explaining the top 3 benefits of owning an electric car for someone living in a city."
This is good, but can be better.
slides.narration:
Let's recall our clear prompt.
It asks to write a short blog post.
This post explains the top 3 benefits of owning an electric car.
It is for someone living in a city.
This is good, but we can make it even better.
We can do this by adding context.
slides.image_prompt: Screenshot of the previous clear prompt, with a subtle 'Can be improved' overlay.

slides.title: Adding Context
content: Let's add context to the prompt.
Who is the audience? What is the purpose?
This helps the AI choose the right tone.
slides.narration:
Now, let's add some context to this prompt.
We need to tell the AI who the audience is.
We also need to state the purpose of the blog post.
This helps the AI choose the right tone and style.
slides.image_prompt: A cartoon person adding sticky notes with 'Audience: Sustainable Living Blog' and 'Purpose: Inform' around the original prompt.

slides.title: Prompt With Context
content: Here's the prompt with context:
"Write a short blog post for a lifestyle blog that focuses on sustainable living. Explain the top 3 benefits of owning an electric car for someone living in a city."
Now the AI knows the audience!
slides.narration:
Here is the prompt with added context.
It asks for a short blog post.
It is for a lifestyle blog focusing on sustainable living.
It should explain the top 3 benefits of owning an electric car.
This is for someone living in a city.
Now the AI knows the specific audience.
It can tailor its response better.
slides.image_prompt: Side-by-side comparison. Left: Clear prompt output. Right: Prompt with context, showing output with a more 'sustainable living' focus.

slides.title: 3. Constraints: Set the Rules!
content: Finally, let's add Constraints.
Constraints are boundaries for the output.
Tell the AI the length, format, and style.
slides.narration:
Finally, let's look at Constraints.
Constraints are like setting rules or boundaries for the AI's output.
You tell the AI the desired length, format, and style of the response.
slides.image_prompt: Cartoon illustration of a person holding a ruler and a stopwatch, indicating 'length' and 'time/format' constraints.

slides.title: Why Constraints are Important
content: Think of a recipe.
It tells you exact measurements and steps.
Constraints guide the AI for precise results.
slides.narration:
Imagine following a recipe.
It gives you exact measurements and steps to get the perfect dish.
Constraints do the same for the AI.
They guide it to produce precise and desired results.
slides.image_prompt: Cartoon of a chef following a recipe book with clear instructions (measurements, steps).

slides.title: Prompt Without Constraints
content: Our prompt with context is good:
"Write a short blog post for a lifestyle blog that focuses on sustainable living. Explain the top 3 benefits of owning an electric car for someone living in a city."
But how long is 'short'?
slides.narration:
Our prompt with context is already good.
But, how long should 'short' be?
What about the tone or format?
These are aspects we can control with constraints.
slides.image_prompt: Screenshot of the prompt with context, with a question mark over the word 'short'.

slides.title: Adding Constraints
content: Let's add specific constraints.
Define word count, tone, and ending.
This makes the output highly specific.
slides.narration:
Let's add specific constraints.
We can define the word count, the tone, and how the post should end.
This makes the AI's output highly specific.
It is tailored to your exact needs.
slides.image_prompt: A cartoon person drawing a box around the prompt, and writing '400 words', 'friendly tone', 'end with question' inside.

slides.title: Prompt With Constraints (Excellent Prompt)
content: Here is an excellent prompt:

"Write a short blog post, under 400 words, for a lifestyle blog that focuses on sustainable living. Explain the top 3 benefits of owning an electric car for someone living in a city. Use a friendly and enthusiastic tone and end with a question to encourage comments."
This prompt is complete and powerful!
slides.narration:
Here is an excellent prompt that includes all three C's.
It asks for a short blog post, under 400 words.
This is for a lifestyle blog focusing on sustainable living.
It should explain the top 3 benefits of owning an electric car.
This is for someone living in a city.
Use a friendly and enthusiastic tone.
End with a question to encourage comments.
This prompt is now complete and powerful!
slides.image_prompt: Side-by-side comparison of the prompt with context output vs. the excellent prompt output, highlighting word count, tone, and concluding question in the latter.

slides.title: Bonus Tip: Provide a Persona
content: Here's a super-powerful trick: use a Persona.
Tell the AI who to be.
It helps the AI adopt a specific role and voice.
slides.narration:
Here is a bonus, super-powerful trick: provide a Persona.
Tell the AI who to be.
This helps the AI adopt a specific role and voice.
Its response becomes more targeted and authentic.
slides.image_prompt: Cartoon illustration of a chameleon changing its color to match its surroundings, symbolizing the AI adopting a persona.

slides.title: Persona Example
content: "Act as an expert travel agent specializing in budget travel. Create a 5-day itinerary for a trip to Rome for a solo traveler who loves history and food."
The AI now acts as an expert!
This ensures a tailored, helpful response.
slides.narration:
For example, you can use a persona.
Say: 'Act as an expert travel agent specializing in budget travel.'
Then: 'Create a 5-day itinerary for a trip to Rome.'
This is for a solo traveler who loves history and food.
The AI now acts as an expert travel agent.
This ensures a tailored and helpful response.
slides.image_prompt: Cartoon of a person in a travel agent's uniform, holding a map of Rome and a brochure, smiling confidently.

slides.title: Summary of Good Prompts
content: Remember the 3 C's:
Clarity: Be specific in your request.
Context: Provide background and audience info.
Constraints: Set rules for length, format, and style.
Bonus: Use a Persona for specific roles.
slides.narration:
To summarize, always remember the 3 C's for good prompts.
These are Clarity, Context, and Constraints.
Clarity means being specific.
Context means providing background.
Constraints mean setting rules.
Don't forget the bonus tip.
Use a Persona for more tailored responses.
slides.image_prompt: A visual summary graphic with three large icons for C's (Clarity, Context, Constraints) and a smaller icon for Persona. Each with a short descriptive text.

First, write a weak prompt for it.
Then, apply Clarity, Context, and Constraints step-by-step to improve it.
Compare the weak and excellent prompt outputs.
Note which 'C' made the biggest difference for you.
slides.narration:
Now as an assignment, pick a simple topic you know well.
First, write a weak prompt for it.
Then, apply Clarity, Context, and Constraints step-by-step to improve it.
Compare the outputs of your weak and excellent prompts.
Finally, note which of the 3 C's made the biggest difference in your results.
